items.title: Wayne Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002
items.q: And I remember distinctly putting down Urbie Green, who was my idol

ctx.x: Well you were in the Sauter-Finegan band, which was really kind of different from most.

Well that certainly was a huge learning experience for me. I had just come out of the service and I auditioned in the same studio, Nola Studios, not the Nola Studios that exists now in New York, but it was a rehearsal studio, a famous rehearsal studio on Broadway around 52nd Street I think it was. And in the same studio I rehearsed, I went up and took an audition for the Sauter-Finegan band, they were looking for a trombone player, and I got the job. And I remember, I’ll never forget, Eddie Sauter coming around…

this time and Woody Herman was paying a hundred and twenty-five a week. No I was making a hundred fifty with Woody Herman. I think the money was about the same to tell you the truth. But it wasn’t that much money to make that much difference. And Kay Finegan, Bill Finegan’s wife, was extremely insulted when I left the band.
